chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: After leaving Ella: Glaser's offer and the Chick Webb memorial concert plan
summary: McRae planned a memorial concert with Moe Gale's backing and star drummers, while considering a move to Joe Glaser.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And then after we got into that, then I was finishing up some things with Artie Shaw. Then we found out that Artie was going to break up his band.
Then -- when Jack Robbins called me one day and says, --

We were ready to go in the second phrase of the things for Artie. Now I'm just gigging and playing, you know, whatever comes up -- somebody want me to do something -- a gig here, I work here for the weekend, I'll do that.
But I didn't have anything (inaudible) especially in mind. I was just trying to finish up -- go back home since I was in town, had left Ella, and go back to Robbins Music.
Because Jack Robbins who was the president
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

of the company, Moe Gale -- hadn't did anything for Moe Gale or Joe Glaser then, but I was a friend of Moe Gale because -- Joe Glaser -- because Joe Glaser had a lot of artist, a lot of black artists.
Like Louie Armstrong, all the different people over there that I knew, because I used to go over there quite a lot.
And Joe would always say, 'Well, what are you going to do now since you left the band. Maybe you'll come sign with me.'
I was in the process of signing an agreement with Joe Glaser -- Associated Booking. I was in agreement to moving over from Moe Gale's office, because I wasn't going to do any more work for Gale.
And I was out of that area. I figured I'm finished with that, now I'm looking around for something what I wanna do.
And in the meanwhile, I wanted to do the Chick Webb memorial concert which I had talked to Moe Gale about.
He had agreed to do it -- put up the
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
money to get it started and everything. And it wasn't fitting for Joe Glaser to put it up. Joe was gonna put up the money to do it, but Joe didn't own the band.
So I said, 'No, let them do it.' Because Chick made them all that money before he died, you know.
And it was an argument -- I'm not afraid to say -- it was an argument that money was left with Moe Gale. And he got mad because I brought this thing up.
I brought the question up, where is Chick's money, because I wanted his sister to get that money because I knew Chick trusted Moe Gale with a lot of money.
And he knew I knew it. That's one thing that --
When I brought that argument up about -- when his sister came in town, I met her, and I said, 'Did you get the money from the office?' She said, 'What money?' I say, 'Well, you know, every time we
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
came in town, Joe Saunders and Chick and myself, we'd go to the office with bags of money -- what it was due do then, and what it --
And Chick told me Moe banked some of his money, you know. Bank his money for him, see.
So, I asked his sister did she get the money and that brought up a whole new thing. And I think that is why I never got to do that Chick Webb Little (Inaudible) concert.
I was gonna use like Cozy Cole, Buddy Rich. I had four different drummers. Four outstanding drummers.
Krupa Gene Cooper -- it was our -- and Cozy Cozy and Buddy Rich. And it was four drummers -- outstanding drummers that I was gonna use.
Louie Jordan was coming back in to do his part. Everybody -- Taft was coming -- everybody Off. was getting (Inaudible).
Benny Carter was coming in to do the arrangements. Don Keelman (Inaudible) was going to do some of the arrangements. (Inaudible).
The publishers -- it goes back to the
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

same thing where we started with Robbins. Jack Robbins was going to get with the publishers and take care all the music -- all the arrangements. Pay all the all the arrangements, (inaudible) music (inaudible).
This was a memorial thing we were supposed to have. We were going to play like ten or fifteen cities.
Everybody was gonna get paid. Just salaries. We're gonna raise all this money for Chick Webb's memorial. Scholarship fund thing, you know.
And when Moe Gale found out that he couldn't handle the money, he backed out. He didn't -- just told Moe Gale -- took off and took a trip around the world, you know.
To get away from it. Told Tim Gale, he say, "Give Teddy five grand to get the thing started." But that was just like to make me feel good while I was sitting in the office.
The next week he gone on a trip around the world. (inaudible).
